description.p: Fincept Terminal is a native C++ desktop financial intelligence terminal featuring real-time market data, AI-powered analytics, multi-broker trading, portfolio management, and 1300+ Python analytics scripts.

ul.li: Real-time crypto and equity trading (Kraken, HyperLiquid, 18+ brokers)
AI chat with multiple LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Ollama)
Python analytics (equity, derivatives, fixed income, quant)
Voice commands via offline Whisper speech recognition
Visual workflow node editor with risk management

description.p: Version 4.5.1 — Plans simplified to Free and Pro ($10/month). New Agent Workbench runs Claude Code and OpenAI Codex inside the terminal with live access to its data, and the terminal can now act as an MCP server for external agents. First-run setup installs in parallel and lets you start working once core libraries are in. A new connector catalog makes 240+ Python data sources browsable and runnable. Faster live tables, charts, logging and instrument search; safer trading with confirmations for live orders, pre-trade risk limits, a kill switch and pending-order expiry; many screen-level fixes across portfolio, news, dashboard and analytics.

Version 4.5.0 — Fixes AI tool calling with Google Gemini: around 150 tools that take a free-form options object were being advertised to Gemini as taking no arguments, so they could be called but never given any input. The assistant now runs a turn's independent tool calls in parallel, while tools that change something still run in order. Long-running work (backtests, quant modules, agent runs) hands back a job you can watch and cancel instead of freezing the conversation, now across ~190 tools rather than a dozen. Tool sequences gain a time limit alongside the step limit and report which ran out. Fixes the AstraFlow providers failing to resolve their endpoint when the base URL was cleared.

Version 4.4.1 — Adds the TickerAll (MetaTrader 5) broker integration for linking and trading MT5 accounts. Python runtime provisioning is more reliable on first run, and the unused FinRL analytics module and its heavy dependencies have been removed.

Version 4.4.0 — Correctness and safety release. Failed data fetches, unreadable settings and incomplete option chains now report an error instead of rendering as confident numbers. Risk limits, order rate limits and the smart/basket order validators are enforced rather than merely configurable. Destructive AI tools are off by default (Settings > Security), live orders require explicit confirmation, and the update manifest is signature-verified.
Version 4.3.0 — MCP long-running tools now run as background jobs the assistant can poll and cancel, and oversized tool results are paged on demand instead of filling the conversation.
Version 4.1.0 — Optional NewsAPI.org news provider, broker-sourced technicals, and fixes.
Version 4.0.0 — Complete rewrite in native C++20 with Qt6.
